recommendations: Do not add Meshroom/AliceVision to Orbit Studio's pipeline yet: mrGSplat (github.com/meshroomHub/mrGSplat) is still a MeshroomHub developer-preview add-on as of mid-2026 -- not installable from Meshroom's UI, needs a manual `rez env meshroom-develop mrGSplat-version` setup plus AliceVision 3.3.0, has only 57 commits and 4 open issues, and its own README admits pose optimization 'didn't really work.' The existing Colab pycolmap + gsplat/Brush path is more mature.

If you ever swap COLMAP for AliceVision's SfM on the pose-estimation step only (skipping mrGSplat entirely), rely on AliceVision's `split360Images`/SplitEquirectangular CLI tool to cube-map the equirectangular stills into perspective sub-images before standard incremental SfM -- this is the same crop-then-reconstruct trick Orbit's ffmpeg reframe step already does, and it is a load-bearing AliceVision feature (in production use since ~2019) rather than the untested direct 'equirectangular' CameraInit tag added in Meshroom 2023.3.0, whose fitness for full multi-position scene SfM (vs. panorama stitching) is unverified.

Do not route the bridge job through OpenSfM expecting a COLMAP handoff: OpenSfM's own `opensfm/actions/export_colmap.py` only maps brown/perspective/fisheye/fisheye_opencv projection types to COLMAP camera models and explicitly raises `ValueError("Can't convert {camera.projection_type} to COLMAP")` for spherical cameras -- there is no built-in bridge from OpenSfM's native spherical reconstruction to the COLMAP text format that Brush/gsplat consume.

For 20 wide-baseline bridge panoramas, if COLMAP 4.1's native SPHERE mode fails, prefer widening/adding more virtual perspective crops per panorama in Orbit's existing ffmpeg-reframe -> pycolmap step over introducing OpenSfM -- OpenSfM's spherical/equirectangular projection type is real and documented (camera_models_overrides.json with a full 360-dataset example) but its GitHub issue history shows the spherical-camera-model issues are old (2018-2022, several still open/unresolved) with no 2026 activity specific to that model, signaling low current maintenance attention for that exact feature.

If native full-360 bundle adjustment (no cropping, keeping full-FOV overlap across only 20 images) is worth the extra integration risk, evaluate a COLMAP-native SPHERE fork such as json87/SphereSfM ('SfM for sphere images in the ERP format within the framework of ColMap') or kiritio-173/colmap-pano instead of OpenSfM -- because these stay inside COLMAP's own binary/text format the whole time, they need no format-conversion bridge to feed pycolmap/gsplat/Brush at all. Verify their license and maintenance status before depending on either, as neither publishes a clear LICENSE file.
slice: Non-COLMAP open photogrammetry stacks with native spherical support: Meshroom 2025.1 mrGSplat and OpenSfM
summary: Meshroom 2025.1.0 (released 2025-08-19, still the latest stable tag as of 2026-07-23; only nightly `develop` builds are newer) restructured AliceVision's node graph into a plugin architecture with sub-process-isolated Python nodes and spun up MeshroomHub (github.com/meshroomHub), a registry of experimental ML plugins including mrGSplat, mrDepthEstimation, MrSegmentation, and others. mrGSplat wraps nerfstudio's gsplat inside Meshroom nodes (PrepareImagesForGSPlat, GaussianSplattingOptim, GaussianSplattingRender, ConvertGSplatModel) but as of mid-2026 remains developer-preview only -- no UI installer, manual rez-env setup, 57 commits, 4 open issues, and a README admitting pose optimization underperforms. Equirectangular/spherical support in AliceVision predates this release: CameraInit gained an "equirectangular" camera-model option in Meshroom 2023.3.0 (2023-12-07), and AliceVision separately ships a split360Images tool that cube-maps panoramas into perspective sub-images for standard SfM -- functionally the same crop-and-reconstruct approach Orbit Studio's ffmpeg step already uses. Meshroom and AliceVision are both MPL-2.0 (confirmed via each repo's LICENSE-MPL2.md/COPYING.md), though optional AliceVision dependencies carry BSD, LGPL, EPL, and MIT licenses. OpenSfM (BSD-2-Clause, copyright mapillary 2014) documents a genuine, production-heritage "spherical" projection type via camera_models_overrides.json, but its own `export_colmap.py` hard-errors (`ValueError`) on spherical cameras -- it only maps brown/perspective/fisheye types to COLMAP formats -- so there is no built-in OpenSfM-to-COLMAP bridge for panorama poses. Recent 2026 OpenSfM issues (Feb/Mar/Apr) are build/dependency bugs, not spherical-model fixes; the spherical-titled issues are all from 2018-2022 and several remain unresolved, suggesting the feature is stable but effectively unmaintained.
uncertainties: mrGSplat's own license was not stated on its GitHub page in the fetched content -- distinct from Meshroom/AliceVision's MPL-2.0, and unconfirmed.

Whether AliceVision's direct 'equirectangular' CameraInit path (vs. split360Images cropping) can actually perform full 6-DOF incremental SfM across multiple moving panorama positions, or is scoped mainly to HDRI panorama stitching/alignment, was not conclusively verified from available docs.

json87/SphereSfM and kiritio-173/colmap-pano license terms were not found in their README content and should be checked directly before use (COLMAP's own license has GPL-encumbered optional components in some builds).

Whether gsplat or Brush (the trainers Orbit already vendors) have any native equirectangular/spherical camera ray model, or would require perspective-crop poses regardless of which SfM stack produces them, was not verified this session.

No official mrGSplat version-numbering or release-tag scheme was found (it appears to track Meshroom develop rather than issuing its own semantic versions), so 'status as of mid-2026' is based on commit/issue counts rather than a dated release note.

sources.title: OpenSfM doc/source/using.rst
key_claims: OpenSfM supports a 'spherical' (legacy name 'equirectangular') projection type for 360 images, configured via camera_models_overrides.json.
Docs point to a full worked example: the 'spherical 360 images dataset'.
export_colmap is listed as a built-in command to 'Export reconstruction to colmap format', but its scope for spherical cameras is not documented at this doc level (verified separately in source).

key_claims: OpenSfM is BSD-2-Clause (Simplified BSD), copyright 2014 mapillary.

sources.title: OpenSfM opensfm/actions/export_colmap.py (via io.py camera mapping)
key_claims: The COLMAP export only maps 'brown'->FULL_OPENCV, 'perspective'->RADIAL, 'fisheye'->RADIAL_FISHEYE, 'fisheye_opencv'->OPENCV_FISHEYE.
Spherical/panorama projection types are not in the mapping table and trigger a raised ValueError instead of a silent skip or a COLMAP SPHERE mapping.
There is therefore no automatic OpenSfM-spherical-to-COLMAP converter available for feeding Brush/gsplat.

sources.title: OpenSfM Issues #1116 and #1119 (2026 activity sample)
key_claims: Feb 12 2026 issue #1116 is about a deprecated matplotlib.cm.get_cmap() call in bin/import_colmap.py and bin/plot_matches.py, unrelated to the spherical camera model.
Apr 2 2026 issue #1119 concerns build/debug-symbol stripping, also unrelated to spherical support.

Spherical-titled issues in the tracker are all from 2018-2022 (#145, #319, #793, #794, #856, #898), with #856 and #898 still open and unresolved, indicating low ongoing maintenance attention specifically to the spherical camera model.

sources.title: SphereSfM README (json87/SphereSfM)
key_claims: SphereSfM is built on top of COLMAP specifically to reconstruct spherical/ERP-format images end-to-end, staying in COLMAP's own format.
No explicit license file/statement found in the README.
No stated minimum-image-count guidance or wide-baseline-specific caveats for small panorama sets like 20 images.
